hints: Look carefully at the positions of the two curves. Which curve is shifted to the right (curve W) and which is more to the left (curve X) at the same partial pressure of oxygen?

Remember the Bohr shift. Higher carbon dioxide lowers pH and reduces haemoglobin affinity for oxygen, so the curve shifts right. At $7.0\text{ kPa}$ oxygen, compare the % saturation of X and W to judge affinity.
walkthrough:
**Observe the shift**

Curve W lies to the right of curve X. At any given partial pressure of oxygen, for example $5$ to $8\text{ kPa}$, curve W shows a lower percentage saturation.

Lower saturation at the same $pO_2$ means oxygen is released more easily.

**Apply the Bohr effect**

More carbon dioxide forms more hydrogen ions and carbonic acid, lowering pH. This reduces haemoglobin affinity for oxygen so oxygen is unloaded in respiring tissues.

Reduced affinity = right shift. Therefore the right-shifted curve W must be the higher carbon dioxide curve. So statement 1 is correct and statement 2 is incorrect.

**Compare affinity at 7.0 kPa**

Draw a vertical line up from $7.0\text{ kPa}$ on the x-axis. Curve X is at about 75% saturation, while curve W is at about 60% saturation.

Higher saturation at the same $pO_2$ means higher affinity. So haemoglobin from curve X has higher affinity than from curve W. So statement 4 is correct and statement 3 is incorrect.

Correct pair is 1 and 4, option B.

options.A: Statement 1 is true but statement 3 is false. At 7.0 kPa, curve W has lower saturation, so lower affinity, not higher.
options.B: Statements 1 and 4 are both true. W is right-shifted by higher carbon dioxide, and X has higher saturation and affinity at 7.0 kPa.
options.C: Both statements are false. Curve X is the lower carbon dioxide curve, and curve W does not have higher affinity at 7.0 kPa.
options.D: Statement 4 is true but statement 2 is false. Curve X is left-shifted, so it represents lower, not higher, carbon dioxide than W.
